correctness.rationale: The leading-mode limit follows from the exact AR(1) symmetric secular equation after the scaling x=N omega, and the limiting DCT overlap follows from exact finite cosine sums. The fixed-mode Robin and eigenvalue limits follow from the source phase equation and Riemann-sum normalization. The correction-factor bound uses orthogonal invariance and a corresponding-row lower bound. Direct covariance diagonalization and exact-frequency calculations reproduce the limiting formulas numerically.

originality.rationale: Prior work contains the finite-N AR(1) eigenstructure, fixed-size rho-to-one DCT endpoint, sinusoidal transform families, performance-equivalence results, continuum Robin eigenproblems, and the recent exact DCT-core KLT factorization. The claim is restricted to the joint N(1-rho) boundary-layer classification, explicit leading-mode angle and iff scale, the resulting quantitative non-uniformity of the recent correction factors, and the basis-angle versus leading-energy-efficiency reconciliation. No matching SCOPE record or accessible external theorem was found. Several older full texts remain uninspected, so originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp dimension-dependent regime where the usual high-correlation DCT approximation ceases to converge in eigenvector geometry and shows that the new exact KLT correction factors can remain an O(1) operator distance from identity despite rho approaching one. The Robin limit explains the mechanism, while the Rayleigh-efficiency formula explains why classical coding-performance conclusions need not contradict the operator-level obstruction.
